vo_splice_map.opening_question_punctuated: Why Do You Weigh Less at Earth's Equator?
vo_splice_map.transcript: Why do you weigh less at Earth's equator? You weigh about half a percent less there. The ground under you is carrying you east at about one and a half thousand kilometers an hour. It is faster than a jet airliner. Earth is about forty-three kilometers wider across the equator. Because the ground at the equator swings round so fast, the whole planet bulges.
